sections.md: Rome bound most Italian communities to itself through treaties, grants of citizenship and Latin colonies planted across the peninsula [E]. After [[Cannae|event]], several southern communities, including [[Capua|place]], went over to Hannibal [E], but the colonies and most of central Italy stayed loyal [E]. Historians debate how far this reflected real attachment to Rome rather than Roman garrisons and fear of reprisals [C].
